newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber ends down sharply on cash concerns.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber ends down sharply on cash concerns.

text.p: Nervous general selling prompted by concern a bill would be presented to Congress to end the U.S. quota on imported Canadaian lumber, on top of a weak cash tone, pushed CME lumber futures to a sharply lower finish, traders said.
Lumber closed down $9.00 to $1.40, paced by limitless May at $394.10 per tbf. July ended $6.30 lower at $389.00.

A group of Congressmen unveiled a bill Thursday to end the quota and fees of between $50 and $100 that Canadian producers were charged when their lumber exports exceed the quota. This came on the heels of reports that the cash lumber market was under further pressure from slow demand.
"Cash prices are back under $390 - and that (bill) is all anybody was talking about today," said Neil Schmaedick, Smith Barney Forest Products analyst.
Backers of the bill say the quota drove up lumber costs and they look for lower housing prices if the bill is passed.
U.S. and Canada agreed that up to 14.7 billion board feet of Canadian lumber can enter the United States duty-free each year with fees charged on shipments above that level.
